FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted draft finalized by the Brushware Sectional Committee Council. by the Bureau of Indian Standards, had been approved by the Chemical after the Division

This standard was first published in 1962. It was based on the requirements for mal-king and grading of bristles as given in the Bristles Grading and Marking Rules, 1950 issued by the Agricultural Marketing Adviser to the Government of India. In the first revision, select quality had been included, 51-44 mm length had been designated as grade. Since the Bristles Grading and Marking Rules, 1972 have been revised, it was deemed revise this standard. In this revision, cut bristles has been included as a quality. necessary to

Bristles are wiry hair - soft, semistiff/stiff, extra stiff in nature, obtained from the back and neck of pigs, hogs, and boars. Bristles are largely used for making various types of brushes such as toilet, clothing, floor polishing, painting, and other industrial purposes. In addition, they are also used for a variety of other purposes, namely, wrapping and covering of cricket balls, and for stitching of shoe soles. for polishing jewellery,

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

X.L.l Burn Test
A 1cW filaments shall be chosen at random. Each single filament of the material when burnt at the tlag-end shall burn with glowing globular mass at the ignited end. Vegetable fibres burn off without this and the burning progresses rapidly towards the other end.

8.1.2 Tapering

Test

A few filaments shall be chosen at random. Each single filament of the material shall be held between the thumb and forefinger midway between the flagend and root-end and rolled with a view to bringing the root-end within the grip. This action in the case trf bristles will be in the direction of the taper thus always getting the flat-end within the grip. X.1.3 In addition to the test5 given in 8.1.1 and 8.1.2, bristles also have a characteristic tearing pattern described below. However, it may be noted that this test is not considered as confirmatory. Therefore, this test shall be carried out in conjunctlon with tests prescribed in 8.1.1 and 8.1.2. X.1.3.1

B-l.1 Apparatus A special, though simple, equipment illustrated in Fig. 2 is used for the preparation of cross sections of the matzial. B-1.1.1 The device used for holding the bristle filaments to be sectioned, consists of portions A and B shown in Fig. 2. Portion A consists of a plate of stainless steel into which is milled a slot 1.27 mm wide. Portion B is the other half of UIP dcvicc. It has a metal tongue on it which fits the slot exactly in width but leaves a gap of 9.5 mm at the closed end. B-1.1.1.1 In addition, the equipment consists of three pushers, marked 6, 7 and 8 shown in Fig. 2. Thcsc fit the slot exactly and will push of the sample to be sectioned until it protrudes 6, 7 and 8 tenth ol millimeter respectively.

ANNEX C (Clause 11.1 )
SAMPLING C-l LOT C-l.1 In any consignment, all the bristles of the same type and grade shall be grouped into 500 bundles or less and each such group shall constitute a lot. C-l.2 The conformity of the bristles in a lot to the requirements of the specification shall be ascertained for each lot separately. Four bundles shall be selected for this purpose from each of the lots separately. C-l.3 The bundles shall be selected at random. To ensure randomness of selection, one of the following procedures, is recommended for use: a) If all the bundles of bristles in a lot are packed in one box, then four bundles may be selected at random from different layers of the same box for analysis. b) If the bundles in a lot are packed in more than one box, approximately equal number of bundles shall be picked up at random from as many boxes as possible so as to obtain a total of four bundles for the lot. C-2 PREPARATION OF SAMPLES OF BRISTLES AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

auarters do not accomDanv it. The four auarters thus Obtained from the b&dle> shall be kep't separately and these shall constitute the individual samples. C-2.2 The four quarters thus obtained from the four bundles may then be homogenized by thorough mixing on a table. The aggregate of bristles shall then be spread out without mixing up the root and flag-ends and shall be divided into an even number of approximately equal heaps, not less than 8 in number. Alternate heaps from these shall be discarded and the remaining heaps shall again be homogenized and the process continued until a final representative composite sample, sufficient for the testing given under C-3.2 is obtained. C-3 NUMBER CONFORMITY OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR

C-3.1 All the individual and composite samples shall be examined for visual characteristics given under 7.1. C-3.2 Determination of the grade and deteclion of natural or dyed bristles (see Amlex B) shall be carried out on the composite sample (SW C-2.2). C-3.3 One of the two tests selected from those given under 8.1 for distinguishing the material from vegetable fibre or hair shall be conducted on two of the individual samples and the other tests on the remaining two individual samples. C-3.4 A lot shall be requirements of this all the tests carried to C-3.3 are found declared as conforming to the specification if the results of out in accordance with C-3.1 to be satisfactory.

C-2.1 Each of the four bundles selected according to C-l.3 shall be marked with a red pencil into four equal parts by drawing two straight intersecting lines at right angles to each other on the root-end of the bundle.
